@oh-my-pi/pi-agent-core

Fixed

  • Enabled native compaction for supported Bedrock Claude models (#16343 by @anatoli-tsinovoy)

@oh-my-pi/pi-ai

Added

  • Added opt-in reclaimAbovePct to auth.accountPolicies: sessions automatically moved to a lower-priority account return to the preferred one once it has that much quota left (#14237 by @will-bogusz)
  • Added reachesBudgetedHost(): whether the catalog's host request budgets (inline image bytes, official image count) apply to a request, true on a model's official endpoint and on Factory Droid's own hosts (#16288 by @will-bogusz)
  • Added Inception API-key login (/login inception) and INCEPTION_API_KEY environment authentication (#16439 by @eggpeat)
  • Added image support for native OpenAI Decisions and Workers AI judgments, prompted vision chat, and auth-gateway System One requests; images exceeding a judgment API's documented caps (e.g. Clef's 4 images, 4 MiB each) are rejected locally (#15471 by @anatoli-tsinovoy).
  • isSurvivingAssistant in providers/transform-messages: whether an assistant turn reaches a replay, malformed tool calls dropped first, so callers outside transformMessages pick the same latest turn (#15791 by @will-bogusz)
  • Broker account-pool files (OMP_AUTH_BROKER_ACCOUNT_POOL_FILE) can hide whole providers and API keys: "*": false makes the file an allow-list, and an entry can be true, false, or { "accounts": [...], "apiKeys": false } (#14235 by @will-bogusz)

Changed

  • cursorRawReadPath() writes a bare start line as raw:N- (file:10 → file:raw:10-), so Cursor exec reads of such a path still read from line N onward now that read takes N:raw as one line (#16438 by @will-bogusz)

Fixed

  • Fixed Anthropic and Bedrock logging one warning per dropped thinking block (hundreds for one request) after a conversation change; the drop now logs one warning with the count (#16392 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed Factory Droid Core models (Kimi, GLM, DeepSeek and others) dropping calls to tools with names over 64 characters and their results from later requests; such names now shorten to 64 characters, and shorter names are sent unchanged (#16384 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed Devin /usage showing no data for accounts signed in with /login devin, and Devin chat sending a failing extra auth request for legacy Windsurf Enterprise keys (#13677 by @will-bogusz)
  • Turns stopped for a thinking loop now keep the tokens and cost the provider had reported, the response id, the request's start time, and its time to first token and duration, instead of recording zero usage and no timing (#16437 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed Claude requests answering a turn whose attachment is a video, PDF, HEIC or other format sent outside a JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP image as if nothing were attached; the turn now fails with an error naming the format (#16407 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed the repeated-tool-call guard missing a loop the model interleaves with a wait that elapses with nothing new; a wait that returns finished work still ends the repetition (#11874 by @dickyudhandika)
  • Fixed Google Antigravity chat and image requests failing with false 429 quota-exhausted errors (#11849 by @jotafurtado)
  • Fixed the stream loop guard never stopping a model stuck repeating punctuation or symbols (?!?!, ✓✓✓) until the output limit; such runs now trip once they repeat for 1 KB, while digit and whitespace runs such as padding and hexdumps are left alone (#14436 by @F0Rextasy)
  • Fixed native remote compaction for supported Bedrock Claude models without changing ordinary Converse turns; a custom non-AWS baseUrl needs remoteCompaction.enabled: true (#16343 by @anatoli-tsinovoy)
  • Fixed Anthropic compaction blocks dropping their signed tool_changes, which made the replayed block fail its signature (#16343 by @anatoli-tsinovoy)

@oh-my-pi/pi-catalog

Added

  • Added native Inception support with Mercury 3, Mercury 2.5, and Mercury 2, live chat-model discovery, API-key login, reasoning controls, and Mercury 3 launch pricing while its catalog reports none; Mercury 3 waits up to 10 minutes for its first output, since high-effort reasoning streams nothing (#16439 by @eggpeat)

Changed

  • Changed Devin model discovery to send legacy Windsurf Enterprise keys unprefixed in one request, dropping the Windsurf-editor retry that returned a smaller model list (#13677 by @will-bogusz)

Fixed

  • Factory Droid now carries Droid's 3.5 MB inline-image budget (inline-image-byte-budget) for its hosted routes, under their 4.5 MB request limit, and the new request-body-byte-limit axis (resolveRequestBodyByteLimit) records that limit; it applies on Factory's own hosts through pi-ai's reachesBudgetedHost (#16288 by @will-bogusz)
  • DeepSeek V4.1 Flash images are now priced by DeepSeek's own billing (994 tokens for a snapcompact frame) instead of a GPT or Claude rate (2,882 to 3,136), so a 25-frame archive no longer counts about 50k tokens the provider never bills and triggers compaction early (#16418 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed Amazon Bedrock Kimi K3 (global./us.moonshotai.kimi-k3) offering Anthropic-style thinking budgets it ignores; it now offers low, high and max effort, defaulting to max (#13697 by @alblez)
  • Marked supported Bedrock Claude models as eligible for native compaction (#16343 by @anatoli-tsinovoy)

@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent

Added

  • bash tool commands now see PI_SESSION_ID and PI_SESSION_FILE, so a script can find the running session's ID and transcript path (#16442 by @johnrichardrinehart and @will-bogusz)
  • Added GitLab merge request support to /review and /annotate code-review: pass an MR URL, pick one mentioned in the conversation, or choose "Review a specific PR/MR" in a GitLab checkout to list open MRs (requires glab); large MRs link per-file diffs through the new mr://<host>/<group>/<project>/<iid>/diff URLs (#16361 by @Shadorain)
  • Added MCP tool progress: tools/call requests ask the server for notifications/progress when the progress can be shown, and updates appear in the running tool card and as an in-place mcp_progress status line in Eval cells, including after auto-backgrounding; request deadlines and Eval timeouts are unchanged (#16431 by @alphastorm)
  • Added image attachments to single and batch eval judge()/judge_batch() calls (local paths or embedded images); image judgments skip candidates without image support and fail explicitly instead of dropping images (#15471 by @anatoli-tsinovoy)
  • Added a job tree to /jobs, /jobs full and the jobs pill's sheet, in the terminal UI and over ACP: subagents' background jobs now appear nested under the task that runs them, with the busiest branches listed first; only your own jobs offer Cancel (#15854 by @H4vC)
  • Added ctx.ui.getEditorComponent() so extensions can wrap the active custom editor factory instead of replacing it (#8655 by @jovi-tsx)
  • omp auth-gateway serve and check can be limited to the providers and API keys the account-pool file allows, using "*": false and "apiKeys": false (#14235 by @will-bogusz)
  • omp usage shows an account's reclaimAbovePct next to its priority and reserve (#14237 by @will-bogusz)

Changed

  • An agent that messages another agent can now wait for the reply instead of erroring; the wait ends early, without an error, once the agent asked finishes its turn without replying or is itself waiting on the caller's result (#16445 by @will-bogusz)
  • Built-in style rule reminders no longer tell the model a user-defined rule matched and it MUST comply; they ask it to check its code against the rule and its exceptions, so models rewrite code a built-in rule allows less often (#16420 by @will-bogusz)
  • read of a SQLite ?q=SELECT … query now accepts &limit= and &offset= and pages the query's rows, as table reads and JSON ?q= reads already do, instead of rejecting the read (#16444 by @will-bogusz)
  • Agents using the browser tool are steered to wait for the text, URL or element they need after a click or navigation instead of sleeping a fixed time, which can finish steps sooner on pages that load content after a variable delay (#16404 by @will-bogusz)
  • The pinned Subagents list shows how many agents are running and the agent hub key, and previews an agent's assignment at full width instead of the first 40 characters of its prompt template (#16486 by @H4vC)

Fixed

  • Fixed auto-QA reports whose tool is a URI (xd://tui: …) being filed under the wrong tool name; a one-line report without : after its tool name is now refused with the format hint (#16278 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed agents guessing conflict://<N> ids for merge conflicts a ranged read didn't show: the warning and the not-found error now point to <path>:conflicts to register them (#16269 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed agents opening your own Chrome through the relay (with browser.relay on) when they asked the browser tool for Chromium with app.tern: false; the tool now points them to app.relay: false (#16294 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed %pip install in Python eval failing with "No module named pip" when the kernel's interpreter is a venv without pip, such as one made by uv venv: it now installs pip into that venv first, with ensurepip or, where that is unavailable, uv (#16300 by @will-bogusz)
  • Reduced HTTP 413 failures on Factory Droid once a session's screenshots and pasted images pass Factory's 4.5 MB request limit: older inline images are now dropped to keep them under 3.5 MB, while the newest message's and newest tool result's images stay when they alone fit the limit; a custom gateway baseUrl is left alone (#16288 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed hashline edits under an older tag overwriting the wrong line when their line numbers came from grep -n, sed -n or a :raw read: a shifted edit whose body matches the current line at those numbers, or that breaks the file's syntax, is now rejected with the current tag and lines (#16383 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed PI_SESSION_FILE in eval cells being a relative path when omp was started with a relative --session-dir (or PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR), so it no longer worked once code changed directory (#16442 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed waking a parked subagent re-sending its whole conversation without the prompt cache whenever other agents had started, finished or parked meanwhile (#15523) (#16369 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed edit accepting changes to lines nothing showed after a stale or unknown tag: a resend under the current tag from the rejection now passes the seen-line check only on the rows that rejection printed (or a retained read showed), so a line seen only through bash is no longer overwritten blind (#16422 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed plugin settings marked secret being readable by other local users in omp-plugins.lock.json; the lockfile is now written owner-only (0600) (#12999, #16368 by @jonasboos)
  • Fixed agents misreading computer.windows() results on their first call (#16299 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed GitLab merge request reads rendering [object Promise] instead of the description (#16477 by @adi-IL)
  • Fixed /restart losing the active named profile and failing to resume its session (#15742 by @sapran)
  • Fixed aborted and timed-out stdio MCP requests continuing to run on the server: OMP now sends notifications/cancelled with the original request id, once and never for initialize, after settling the call and without waiting on the pipe (#16430 by @alphastorm)
  • Fixed the agent restarting on its own after you stopped it with Esc whenever a background subagent or job finished; the result is recorded in the transcript and the agent waits for your next message
  • Fixed Mnemopi memory completions ignoring the memory role's thinking suffix, including one inherited from tiny or smol when modelRoles.memory is unset; each retry.fallbackChains.memory entry sends its own level, and :off disables reasoning (#16378 by @alphastorm)
  • Fixed MCP tools running a call twice when the server connection dropped mid-request: a stdio request already written to the server, or an HTTP or legacy SSE request whose connection reset or closed after it was sent, now fails as non-retryable with a diagnostic saying it may have run, instead of being replayed after a reconnect; requests that never left OMP, including refused connections, still reconnect and retry once (#16429 by @alphastorm)
  • Fixed /move path completion jumping into a subfolder on Tab: .., ., and ~ now complete to ../, ./, and ~/ before listing their children, a trailing \ lists a folder on Windows, absolute Windows paths (C:/…) are no longer rewritten as relative paths, and the project directory is offered as ./ instead of /
  • Fixed edit blaming boundary indentation when a one-row replacement only fails because its body ends with a trailing comma (e.g. the last element of a JSON array); the error now names the comma (#16423 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed a timed-out browser selector action dropping its match count without a word when omp could not count the matches; the error now says why (#16389 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed every session in a project without .vscode/mcp.json logging a "[VS Code] Failed to read …/.vscode/mcp.json" warning; a missing file is now skipped silently, while an unreadable or unparsable one still warns (#16434 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed agents opening pages in your own signed-in Chrome when browser.relay is on and you asked for a throwaway browser (#16390 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed the built-in ts-no-tiny-functions and ts-promise-with-resolvers rules reminding you about code they allow: exported functions, public class and object members, type guards, if/try/catch blocks, and never-settling new Promise(() => {}) (#16419 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed read losing the last lines of a comma list that pairs ranges with a tail (file:1-30,-30, file:1-30,:-30), and erroring on the same list for artifact:// and other internal URLs; both parts are now read (#16435 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed edit rejecting a placeholder tag (#AUTO, #????), a missing tag, or a header with no ops without naming the file's current tag; these now get the same reply as an unknown tag, so the retry can use that tag instead of a read (#16425 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed read line ranges and tails (:9-11, :-50) of macOS .sample.txt reports and .cpuprofile files returning lines of the generated profile summary instead of the file, so edits from them were rejected as stale; the summary now appears only on a whole-file read, without line numbers (#16397 by @will-bogusz)
  • Models whose provider strips images from requests, such as DeepSeek V4 Flash on Venice or NanoGPT, now get text compaction and text-only image handling like text-only models; snapcompact archived onto frames that reached them as [image omitted] placeholders, and history images were still processed and uploaded before being dropped (#16436 by @will-bogusz)
  • Line range reads of ssh://, URLs and other in-memory resources no longer return only the line above the range when that line fills the 50KB budget; the page now starts at the requested line, and byte-limit notices state the 50KB limit instead of the bytes shown (#16391 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed Auto-QA grievances sharing your home directory and login name with the qa.omp.sh collector; paths under your home are sent as ~/…, and the login name inside labels and paths as <user>, including reports recorded before this fix (#16409 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed the computer tool's control.acquire prompt, left unanswered, failing the whole call with "Computer code execution timed out"; the prompt now expires shortly before the timeout and the call returns reason: "unanswered" (#16388 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed reads whose optional leading context line exceeded the byte budget returning only the oversized-line notice or a preview of that context line and hiding the requested lines; the read now retries from the requested start without leading context (#16485 by @adi-IL).
  • Fixed read path:N:raw (and :raw:N, URLs included) returning a page from line N instead of the one line N; grep on internal and web URLs now filters :N:raw to that line too, and :N-:raw still runs on from N (#16438 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed Anthropic web search answers breaking into separate paragraphs at every citation, with sentences split mid-way and lines starting with . (#16396 by @a-glapinski)
  • Fixed custom tools that import an @oh-my-pi/* package (such as @oh-my-pi/pi-natives or @oh-my-pi/pi-utils) failing to load with "Cannot find package" in the installed omp binary; they now get the host's copy, as extensions already did (#16421 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed resuming a session selecting an abandoned branch after a late off-branch entry such as a background bash result; off-branch entries now record the active leaf they interrupted and replay restores it (#16483 by @adi-IL).
  • Fixed hashline REM deleting and MV moving a file under an invented or stale tag; a bare file op now needs the file's current tag, like a line edit (#16381 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed write deleting the leading numbers of every line in content such as hex dumps, disassembly and timestamped logs; it now removes copied read line numbers only when they count up by one, as read and grep print them (#16441 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed auto thinking chosen for the DEFAULT role in the /model hub reverting to the model's default effort (e.g. max on Z.AI glm-5.3) on the next launch (#16370, #16398 by @alvadorn)
  • Fixed Google Antigravity web search failing with false 429 quota-exhausted errors (#11849 by @jotafurtado)
  • Fixed omp exiting to the shell when the model picker (Alt+P) or model hub opened after compatibility extensions loaded (#12293, #12653 by @wolfiesch)
  • Fixed todo lists set over RPC set_todos disappearing when the session is reloaded, resumed, or compacted; RpcClient.setTodos() sends the command (#12590 by @anthonyrisinger)
  • Fixed batch task calls silently running the default agent when a specialist such as reviewer, scout, or a custom agent was set at the top level instead of in tasks[].agent; the call is now rejected with that guidance (#12610 by @dbc-hbin)
  • Fixed sessions started before an omp upgrade losing word completion and restarting the shared word-completion daemon every 30 seconds, which reloaded its model for every session on the new version; they now use the newer daemon (#15610) (#16380 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed supported Bedrock Claude models falling back to soft instead of remote compaction (#16343 by @anatoli-tsinovoy)
  • Fixed browser tab.run(fn, [url]) and browser.open("https://…") failing with a bare "expects an options object"; the errors now say to pass { args: [...] } and browser.open({ url, name }) (#16236 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed the built-in ts-set-map, ts-import-type and ts-no-any rules reminding you about code they allow: an empty or computed Set/Map, a runtime await import(), or the word "any" in a comment (#16242 by @will-bogusz)

@oh-my-pi/pi-mnemopi

Fixed

  • Fixed background fact extraction storing only the first 5 facts of a plain-line extractor answer; it now keeps up to 20, matching JSON answers (#16377 by @alphastorm)

@oh-my-pi/pi-natives

Changed

  • Reduced native Git diff allocation overhead (#16349 by @kyle-elliott)
  • Reduced native memory-reranking allocations when candidate text contains repeated words (#16348 by @kyle-elliott)
  • Reduced allocation overhead when collecting directory grep results, including paginated searches (#16226 by @kyle-elliott)
  • Token counting for OpenAI, Qwen, DeepSeek, Kimi, GLM and Jev models is 11-30% faster on English text, code and Markdown (#16399 by @will-bogusz)

Fixed

  • Fixed index.d.ts drifting from the generated bindings, so building the natives no longer leaves the checkout modified (#16306 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed cargo test writing crash reports from panicking Rust tests into your real ~/.omp/logs: they now go to a per-user pi-natives-test-logs-<uid>/ under the OS temp dir (#16386 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed the bash tool's rm -rf reporting No such file or directory for entries another process removed first and leaving the parent directories behind; under -f an entry already gone now counts as removed, as in GNU rm (#16433 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed the bash tool's rg -c and rg --count-matches printing path:0 for every file without a match; zero counts are now printed only with --include-zero, as in ripgrep (#16432 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed ln -s local://… <path> in the bash tool creating a host symlink that holds the URL text, which nothing can follow; a symlink on the host to a file-backed URL now stores the file it stands for (#16428 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed macOS background input leaving the target app in front of yours when it came forward just as you clicked another window of your app; your app comes back with the window you clicked (#16217 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed omp sessions on macOS adding a terminal icon to the Dock after the computer tool listed displays (#13455 by @VelizarSeleznev)

@oh-my-pi/snapcompact

Fixed

  • Fixed snapcompact archive frames for Factory Droid models ignoring Factory's inline-image budget: they are now sized to half of it, like other budgeted hosts (#16288 by @will-bogusz)

@oh-my-pi/pi-tui

Added

  • Added mergeLineRanges and an optional BareLineMode argument to parseLineRanges ("single" reads a lone bare N as that one line) (#16435 by @will-bogusz)

Changed

  • selectorLineRanges() reads a bare N compounded with raw (17:raw, raw:17) as the single line N; parseLineRanges() takes an optional "single" mode for the same rule (#16438 by @will-bogusz)
  • Collapsed wait cards show one row per finished job (or a single "waiting on N jobs" line) instead of re-printing the whole job tree on every poll; Ctrl+O shows the full tree (#16486 by @H4vC)
  • Bash cards show the elapsed time while a command runs, and wall time, timeout and backgrounded job in the bottom border instead of a separate ⟨…⟩ line (#16486 by @H4vC)
  • The terminal /jobs sheet shows the selected job's full command (#16486 by @H4vC)
  • Grep, glob, find, IRC message, and proc:///agent:///cfg:// result rows start at the same column as other tool rows (#16486 by @H4vC)

Fixed

  • Fixed Tern sessions logging TSP: terminal stopped acknowledging frames every 5 seconds for as long as the terminal stops acknowledging frames; it now warns once per stall and logs the stall's length when acknowledgements resume (#16393 by @will-bogusz)
  • splitPathAndSel and splitInternalUrlSel peel comma line lists that include a tail chunk (:1-12,-15) or repeat the colon after a comma (:1-30,:-30, also beside :raw); splitPathAndSel(path, { foldListColons: false }) keeps the repeated colon in the path (#16435 by @will-bogusz)
  • Generic tool cards now reveal the complete result when expanded (#15335 by @yuzu-octopus)
  • Added footerMeta to OutputBlockOptions and ToolCardSnapshot to draw short facts inside a frame's bottom border (#16486 by @H4vC)
  • Fixed markdown table rows shattering at narrow widths when a wide glyph sat in a one-cell column; the glyph is now clamped to its column instead of re-wrapping the row (#16479 by @adi-IL).
  • Fixed charts in answers drawing as blank bands, on screen and in scrollback, when iTerm2 drew them in a background tab; inline images now carry an explicit height in rows (#16471 by @galtamam-cmyk)
  • Fixed an inline image (such as a table's chart) disappearing in iTerm2 when new output pushed it past the top of the screen; it now moves to scrollback whole (#16467 by @galtamam-cmyk)
  • Fixed inline images, hyperlinks, notifications and styled underlines staying off in iTerm2 sessions reached over SSH, where the forwarded LC_TERMINAL marker was ignored (#16450 by @yuzu-octopus)
  • Added Eval mcp_progress status events, updated in place per call and evictable under the status-event cap, plus formatMCPProgress() and MCPToolDetails.progress for MCP progress display (#16431 by @alphastorm)

@oh-my-pi/pi-utils

Breaking Changes

  • readTarEntriesFromBuffer() in @oh-my-pi/pi-utils/ar/tar now returns Promise<ArchiveIndexEntry[]> instead of ArchiveIndexEntry[]; await its result (#16394 by @will-bogusz)

Added

  • Added maxStreamSize to ArchiveLimits (default 4 GB): the most a large .tar.gz or .tar.zst may decompress in one pass, so a decompression bomb fails instead of running without bound (#16394 by @will-bogusz)

Fixed

  • Fixed bun test runs writing their logs into your real ~/.omp/logs: test processes now log to a per-user omp-test-logs-<uid>/ under the OS temp dir (#16386 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed .tar.gz and .tar.zst archives that decompress past 256 MB failing to list or read with a raw Cannot create a Buffer larger than … error; a bare .gz or .zst that large now names the archive size limit (#16394 by @will-bogusz)
  • Fixed frontmatter repair deleting HTML comments from document bodies and plain markdown; it now strips only leading comments ahead of the opening delimiter, so prompt bodies keep their comments (#16481 by @adi-IL).

FlashML-org/FreeToken ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v0.2.0 Stable2026-10-21T00:37:56Z

Highlights

  • GGUF Support. llama.cpp GGUF files serve directly with ft serve --model <local file>.gguf; quantized tensors run on llama.cpp's own kernels (ggml-cuda on the GPU, ggml-cpu for hybrid / cpu experts). Supported GGUF archs:
    • qwen2 (Qwen2 / Qwen2.5), qwen3 and qwen3moe (Qwen3 dense and MoE)
    • qwen35 and qwen35moe (Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 dense and MoE, Qwen3.8-27B), qwen4exp (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next)
    • gemma4 (Gemma-4 12B, 26B-A4B, 31B)
    • llama (Llama 3.x, and Mistral files converted before llama.cpp's mistral3 arch)
    • muse-glimmer (Muse-Glimmer)
    • minimax-m2 (MiniMax-M2 / M2.x), minimax-m3 (MiniMax-M3)
    • glm4moe (GLM-4.5, GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.6, GLM-4.7), glm5-next (GLM-5.3-Flash)
  • Support new models.
    • DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, text and images (#603)
    • Image input for DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (#502)
  • Faster NVFP4 on sm_120 (RTX 50xx, RTX PRO Blackwell). NVFP4 checkpoints with static activation scales run on NVFP4 activations (W4A4): at 128 or more tokens per expert the MoE layer is 2.54x faster on the RTX PRO 6000 and 3.72x on the RTX 5090 (#736), and Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 and Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4 reach the first token 1.6x to 2.7x faster at 1k to 8k prompt tokens (#737).

GGUF Support

FreeToken now serves llama.cpp GGUF checkpoints (#690). Quantized tensors keep the ggml type they have in the file and run on llama.cpp's kernels, vendored from llama.cpp 8c2134a8: ggml-cuda MMQ / MMVQ on the GPU, and ggml-cpu row kernels for experts on the CPU (#704). The model config, chat template and stop tokens come from the file's metadata.

  • Weight types (per tensor; a file preset such as Q4_K_M or UD-Q8_K_XL mixes several):
    • Supported: F32, F16, BF16; Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0, Q5_1, Q8_0; Q2_K, Q3_K, Q4_K, Q5_K, Q6_K; IQ1_S, IQ2_XXS, IQ2_XS, IQ2_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ3_S, IQ4_NL, IQ4_XS; MXFP4, NVFP4; Q1_0, Q2_0. The layers of one file may use different types, and an expert layer may pair a float projection with a quantized one (#702).
    • NVFP4 GGUFs converted from ModelOpt checkpoints carry per-tensor .scale tensors; the gemma4, llama, qwen3, qwen3moe, qwen35 and qwen35moe loaders apply them on dense linears and on every MoE strategy (#732).
    • Not supported yet: IQ1_M (no MMQ kernel); NVFP4 token embeddings; NVFP4 .scale tensors in qwen2, qwen4exp, muse-glimmer, minimax-m2, minimax-m3 and glm4moe files (refused at load); --dtype float16 with NVFP4 .scale tensors; TQ1_0 and TQ2_0; Q4_0_4_4 / Q4_0_4_8 / Q4_0_8_8, which llama.cpp has removed; types defined only in llama.cpp forks such as ik_llama.cpp; expert layers whose gate and up projections use different types.
  • MoE strategies: fused and offload for every type (#690); hybrid and cpu for every type on x86-64 CPUs, where ggml-cpu picks the best of llama.cpp's x86 CPU builds at startup (#704). Layers of different types get their own slot pools in the expert cache (#689, #700); cpu refuses files whose expert layers use several types. ft bench bw --model <file>.gguf measures the hybrid fetch split for each expert layer kind (#734).
  • scripts/gguf_check/ in the source tree checks whether GGUF files load (config, weights, kernel coverage, chat template) from header-only stubs, without downloading the weights (#756).
  • Weights past the 32-bit block offsets of MMQ / MMVQ raise instead of running (#699).
  • Not supported yet: image input (mmproj files), Gemma-4 E2B / E4B, the mistral3 arch, Mixtral, GLM-4.7-Flash (deepseek2 arch), glm4moe files with a fused attn_qkv, tensor parallelism.

Supported architectures

Family GGUF arch PR

Qwen3 dense, Qwen3 MoE qwen3, qwen3moe #707
Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 dense and MoE, Qwen3.8-27B qwen35, qwen35moe #701
Qwen3.8-Flash-Next qwen4exp #690
Gemma-4 26B-A4B (every ggml type; was Q4_0 only) gemma4 #690
Gemma-4 12B, 31B gemma4 #706
Llama 3.x, Mistral (files converted before llama.cpp's mistral3 arch) llama #722
Muse-Glimmer muse-glimmer #724
MiniMax-M2 / M2.x, MiniMax-M3 minimax-m2, minimax-m3 #725
GLM-4.5, GLM-4.5-Air, GLM-4.6, GLM-4.7 glm4moe #731
GLM-5.3-Flash glm5-next #721

Model Support

  • Support DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (DeepseekV41ForCausalLM), text and images (#603)
    • --swa-decoder-replay bounded|exact: bounded (default) is the tech report's decoder SWA replay, exact runs the decoder on every prompt token
    • The two Engram tables stream from the checkpoint shards on demand
    • reasoning_effort takes low / high / max; a 1-100 budget goes through chat_template_kwargs; DSML tool calls are parsed
  • Image input for DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (DeepseekV4ForCausalLM) (#502)
  • Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8-27B: add the zero-centred norm weights' +1 in fp32 at runtime, as transformers does, instead of folding it into the bf16 weight (#755)
  • Qwen3.8-Flash-Next:
    • Serve the model card's 1M-token YaRN recipe through --hf-overrides (#573)
    • Reduce QSA block top-k candidates past 16 splits: the per-layer top-k of one decode step at ~985k tokens of context goes from 845 to 45 µs on an RTX 3090 Ti (#571)
    • Load compressed-tensors exports (per-channel fp8 dense layers, NVFP4 experts) and bf16 PLE tables (#759)
    • Fence disk PLE staging against in-flight lookups (#588)
  • Keep the Muse-Glimmer attention gate as its own linear next to qkv_proj (#741)
  • Preserve the GLM-4 router correction bias in fp32 (#469)
  • Raise WeightLoadError when the checkpoint cannot be read (#518)
  • Add scripts/checkpoint_diagnose/ to the source tree: tells whether FreeToken or the checkpoint is at fault when an HF checkpoint does not load, and fixes a non-standard local checkpoint after showing the plan (#762)

Quantization

  • Keep NVFP4 weight global scales in fp32. They were converted to fp16, where many of them fell in the subnormal range (#739).
  • On sm_120 (RTX 50xx, RTX PRO Blackwell), NVFP4 checkpoints with static activation scales (ModelOpt NVFP4, compressed-tensors NVFP4) run on NVFP4 activations (W4A4):
    • MoE prefill from 4 tokens per expert: at 128 or more tokens per expert the MoE layer is 2.54x faster on the RTX PRO 6000 and 3.72x on the RTX 5090 (geomean over 9 model shapes) (#736)
    • Linears: W4A4 prefill and new W4A16 kernels for decode; time to first token at 1k to 8k prompt tokens is 1.6x to 2.7x faster on Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4 and Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4 (#737)
    • --quant-backend moe.nvfp4=triton and linear.nvfp4=triton keep W4A16

Engine

  • Split the offload expert cache into slot pools: --moe-cache-scope unified|per-layer, --moe-cache-split equal|profile:<path>, and --moe-cache-mem to size the cache in memory (#689)
  • Serve models whose MoE layers use different expert formats, one slot pool per format (#700)
  • --moe-strategy fused serves NVFP4 and MXFP4 experts through the expert banks (#601)
  • Serve block-FP8 experts on the cpu and hybrid strategies (#662)
  • ft bench bw --model <checkpoint> benches every MoE layer kind of a GGUF or HF checkpoint, and hybrid takes its fetch split per layer (#734)
  • Page-locked expert banks: when pinned memory is capped, hybrid with --moe-cpu-layers OS-locks the expert banks past the pin limit, and the locked layers keep GPU slots and fetch part of their misses through a pinned staging buffer. This also works for models whose expert layers need several slot pools, such as GGUF files that mix expert types. Adds --moe-locked-fetch, --moe-locked-max-fetch and --moe-collect-stats (#742)
  • Spin-wait the CPU MoE pool between layers: +20% batch-1 hybrid decode on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-NVFP4 (H100) (#619)
  • Split hybrid decode routes inside the ensure kernel (#685)
  • Split the CPU MoE executor into weight formats and GPU sync backends (#670)
  • Widen the expert gather on NVLink-C2C hosts (GH200 / GB200 / GB300): 222 → 412 GB/s on GH200 (#610)
  • Upload CUDA graphs at capture so a stream wait cannot block the first launch (#697)
  • Under overlap scheduling, requests now end with max_tokens tokens instead of one fewer (#546)
  • Preserve greedy sampling in mixed batches (#471)
  • Clone inserted radix keys to release request buffers (#559)

Kernels

  • Rewrite the Triton NVFP4 MoE prefill GEMM: 6.6x to 16.1x faster; Gemma-4 26B-A4B NVFP4 prefill with fused goes from 5,571 to 35,732 tok/s at 4.6k tokens on H100 (#723)
  • Speed up the NVFP4 MoE prefill GEMM on RTX GPUs: a warp-specialized Gluon kernel on sm_120, 1.50x faster per MoE layer at 8192 tokens on the RTX PRO 6000 (geomean over 6 model shapes) (#733); pipelined scale loads on GeForce sm_86 / sm_89 (#735)
  • Split Triton decode attention by context length and SM count: batch-1 decode at 128k on H100 goes from 77 to 174 tok/s on Gemma-4 26B-A4B and from 90 to 213 tok/s on gpt-oss-20b (#729)
  • Copy Triton attention metadata without blocking the host (#726)
  • Rework kernels that Triton 3.8 compiles slower: NVFP4 MoE decode (#631), Triton extend attention and Gemma-4 sliding-window decode (#632), DeepSeek-V4 sparse attention and gated pool (#633), the DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer (#634), and block-FP8 MoE decode and the gpt-oss MXFP4 GEMV (#653)
  • Avoid NaN in the Triton sampling softmax when a chunk starts with -inf (#654)
  • Correct JIT tensor matcher checks and PDL arch guards (#638)
  • Pin the tvm-ffi JIT arch to the bound GPU (#521)

Server and CLI

  • Add --api-key authentication to ft serve; ft shell, ft ctl, ft launch and ft daemon send the key (#639)
  • Keep Anthropic inline system messages in place for prefix reuse; --anthropic-inline-system auto|preserve|fold (#608)
  • Apply presence_penalty and frequency_penalty (#527)
  • Add --hf-overrides JSON to override the checkpoint config, with vLLM's semantics (#573)
  • Accept file://localhost/... URIs for local media (#758)
  • Report the backend KV page size in /v1/stats (#599)

AMD ROCm (WIP, experimental)

  • Build from source and run on RDNA3 and RDNA4 GPUs; tested on gfx1100 and gfx1201 (#132, #587)
  • Gate CUDA-only optional backends on ROCm; FlashInfer, sgl_kernel and vLLM kernels fall back to the built-in kernels (#134)
  • cpu and hybrid MoE sync with the GPU through HIP stream memory operations (#670)
  • Clamp the QSA KV tile to the device LDS budget on RDNA (#587)
  • Avoid a Triton 3.8 miscompile of the MoE alignment on ROCm (#691)

Dependencies

  • torch >=2.14,<2.15 (was >=2.11,<2.12), torchvision >=0.29,<0.30, Triton >=3.6,<3.9 (was ==3.6.0), sglang-kernel 0.4.9 (was 0.4.5); source builds compile the C++ extensions as C++20 (#630).
  • transformers >=5.18,<5.19 (was >=5.16,<5.17) (#698).
  • flashlib 0.4.0 (was 0.3.0) and numpy <3 (was <2.5); numba is no longer installed (#669).
  • [fi] pins flashinfer-python 0.6.18.post1 (was >=0.6,<0.7), and install.sh installs flashinfer-python, -cubin and -jit-cache at that one version (#545).
  • The gguf package is no longer a dependency; gguf-py is vendored (#690).
  • sglang-kernel resolves from PyPI; the sglang wheel index is dropped (#524).
  • install.sh writes FREETOKEN_HOME to environment.d instead of FREETOKEN_FT_BIN (#576).

Breaking Changes & Deprecations

  • Some FTW checkpoints converted by older builds must be reconverted with ft checkpoint:
    • experts converted with --moe-backend fused or triton are dense and no longer load; ft checkpoint now always writes experts as banks (--moe-backend is kept for compatibility) (#601)
    • NVFP4 FTWs that store the global scales as fp16 are refused at load (#739)
    • Muse-Glimmer FTWs with the attention gate fused into qkvg_proj no longer load (#741)
    • Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.6 / Qwen3.8-27B FTWs load without an error but give wrong output: their norm weights hold the +1 already (#755)
  • FREETOKEN_API_KEY in the environment of ft serve now turns authentication on (#639).
  • ft bench bw profiles from older builds are ignored; rerun ft bench bw, with --model <checkpoint> to cover every layer kind. A layer without a matching row fetches at most 1 expert per step under hybrid (#662, #734).
  • --moe-strategy auto no longer switches to hybrid from the ft bench bw profile; pass --moe-strategy hybrid (#734).

Contributors

"You're gonna need a bigger boat." — Brody, 《Jaws》 (1975)

✨ What's New

Feature Description By
Folders on Claude and DeepSeek (off by default) Turn on Claude · Folders or DeepSeek · Folders under Plugins to file chats into folders in the sidebar, as on ChatGPT. —
A quieter, unified look The popup, Prompt Manager, export, timeline, highlights, folders and other panels share one calmer style that follows each site's light or dark theme; the Voyager name is drawn as a new wordmark. —
Local Bridge answers ChatGPT's approval card When ChatGPT asks to allow Google Drive or another app, Voyager CLI's --approve-apps lets the extension click it for you (CLI 0.4.0 or later). —
Local Bridge saves reply files Files a ChatGPT reply offers are saved next to the reply by Voyager CLI (CLI 0.3.0 or later). —
Exact numbers in settings Settings with a wide range get a number box beside the slider, so you can type the exact value. PR #1062 by @ccch1mneyyy

🐛 Bug Fixes

Fix Description By
Gemini: exporting very long chats A very long conversation no longer fails to export; Voyager exports the loaded part and says only the most recent part is included. —
Gemini: selecting replies to export Reply checkboxes show again, no longer cover the first words, and line up in one column. —
Gemini: folders above Notebooks After Gemini's sidebar change, folders can again sit above Notebooks or above your chats. —
ChatGPT export button The header export button lines up with Share and no longer covers it while a dialog is open. —
ChatGPT Local Bridge A failed send takes its prompt back out of the input box, a prompt with a Google Drive link sends normally, and a reply cut short by a dropped connection is no longer saved as the answer. —
Folder details The folder arrow no longer turns into a dash, all seven colors fit on one row, sort options wrap in a narrow settings menu, and DeepSeek's select-chats button is no longer covered. —
Prompt Manager after an update Updating or reloading the extension no longer leaves the Prompt Manager's button and panel behind on the page. —

thedotmack/claude-mem ↗ 2 releases · 2 stable
v15.0.1v15.0.1 — Consistent Smart recall across merged projects Stable2026-10-20T22:40:29Z

Keep Smart recall consistent across merged projects

Smart search, timeline context, and selected observation details now use the same checkout project scope. An observation found through a merged project alias remains available in the next two steps, instead of incorrectly returning “not found.”

  • Resolves the same project read keys for search results, explicit timeline anchors, query-selected timeline anchors, and selected observation reads.
  • Keeps adopted records visible while excluding unrelated or unadopted records and respecting platform-source filters.
  • Preserves the Smart default three-step workflow and the optional dumb_search alternative introduced in 15.0.0. No API or schema migration is required.

Regression coverage includes real HTTP/SQLite cases that fail on 15.0.0 and pass with this repair, plus related scope-isolation checks.

View release →

v15.0.0v15.0.0 — Smart memory search by default Stable2026-10-20T21:52:33Z

Smart memory search by default

Memory recall now defaults to Smart: search the compact index, inspect context around relevant results, then fetch only the selected details. The agent reasons about relevance between these three steps. Local, cloud/Pro, and standalone-server instructions describe the tools available in that runtime.

The optional one-call lookup is now dumb_search. Its description is explicit: “Doesn’t reason about the results. Fast, but shallow. Use Smart for reliable recall.” It performs deterministic title matching and does not reason about relevance.

Migration

  • Use the mem-search skill for default Smart recall. Local tools are search → timeline → get_observations; Cloud/Pro starts with memory_search and can fetch selected summaries with get_summaries.
  • Replace calls to the old mem_search guided/auto API and flash_search with the Smart workflow, or explicitly choose dumb_search for a shallow lookup. Auto/guided modes and continuation cursors are removed.
  • Refresh existing MCP connections so clients load the new tool catalog and descriptions.

Correctness

  • Cloud timeline supports context anchored to a selected search result.
  • Standalone-server recall stays scoped to its configured server project rather than reading a local worker's memory.
  • Selected-detail output reports its bounds honestly and preserves selected record identities when long content must be shortened.
  • Native memory lookup uses observation-only indexes, and mixed local indexes retain session/prompt ID prefixes so follow-up reads cannot select a different record kind with the same number.
  • Installer prompts, public documentation, integration instructions, and generated memory guidance use the same Smart-first policy.

Other changes since v14.0.1

  • Added Hermes Agent memory support and installation, including safe handling of existing YAML configuration.
  • Added fallback between an Anthropic API key and the Claude subscription, with quota classification and recovery back to the primary provider at a message boundary.
  • Kept worker HTTP requests responsive during local context reads, bounded broad full-text fallback searches, and removed quadratic tag-stripping stalls.
  • Improved memory correctness: type="all" searches every category, deleted observations remove their Chroma documents, unexpected Chroma exits reject pending requests, and failed Windows checkpoint renames preserve the previous checkpoint.
  • Tightened privacy and request handling: fully private prompts no longer become stored user requests; key redaction handles trailing dashes; internal Grok research briefs do not become user work; multilingual work requests are recognized; and OpenRouter field condensation avoids unnecessary reasoning.
  • Improved installation and runtime reliability across Windows, macOS, Conda, Qoder, Goose, OpenCode, Antigravity, Codex, and TeamBrain. Fixes include launcher self-recursion and working-directory handling, stale temporary-directory cleanup, actionable authentication and missing-runtime errors, and correct host hook registration.
  • Added optional cross-project context with CLAUDE_MEM_CONTEXT_PROJECTS=all, corrected folder context ordering and glob matching, expired orphaned summary spool entries, and improved effective-data-directory log lookup and cloud authentication telemetry.

Validation and delivery identities are recorded separately in the release receipt after the final builds, deployment, and package checks complete.

different-ai/openwork ↗ 2 releases · 1 stable · 1 prerelease
v0.18.59OpenWork v0.18.59 Stable2026-10-20T22:32:16Z

Read, edit, and discuss documents in Workbot

  • Work on documents without leaving Workbot. When Documents is enabled for your workspace, preview Drive files before choosing Edit when editing is enabled, keep chat open beside a document, and continue your conversation with the file in view. Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides stay in Google and save to the original; on OpenWork Cloud, Office files can use an editor in your own workspace when enabled.
  • AI models and providers work more smoothly across OpenWork. Desktop users can use existing Azure Foundry and custom OpenAI-compatible providers on OpenCode v2, see organization model changes in the picker when enabled, and find the same available models in Settings and shortcuts. When AI Gateway access is enabled, cloud agents can use supported models assigned by their organization.
  • Admins can check setup before work gets stuck. Settings › Diagnostics brings desktop startup, AI provider, connector, and deployment-service checks together. Google Workspace settings can also identify APIs an admin needs to turn on, and Workbot explains when an organization needs an AI provider before it can answer.
  • Chat keeps files, prompts, and agent work on track. Files saved from chat go to the opened folder, including files created in a conversation's own folder; links with spaces open correctly, failed writes are labeled as failed, and messages in side chats are easier to start. OpenCode v2 history copies can resume after restart; if a chat is too large to copy whole, its largest outputs or attachments stay in the original history.
  • Team and Workbot tasks have clearer paths. When enabled, members can connect assigned accounts in Workbot; members with team-management access can open the right team's settings, and teams can follow tasks started on another computer. When available, admins can set team or organization defaults for new desktop chats and provider-specific spend limits, and inspect Library use and free Auto conversion insights. Workbot's link-only sharing is gone; authorized invitation emails remain available in Den.
  • Self-hosting and connected tools get practical fixes. Self-hosters get updated AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure deployment options and clearer service checks. MCP clients can identify OpenWork and receive clearer tool guidance, and the website's Trust Center links now lead to the hosted Trust Center.

Full changelog: https://openworklabs.com/docs/changelog · Compare

CloakHQ/CloakBrowser ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
chromium-v155.0.8059.39.1-proChromium v155.0.8059.39.1 — Stealth Build (Pro) Stable2026-10-20T18:15:39Z

CloakBrowser Pro: Stable advances to Chromium 155.0.8059.39.1 (all platforms)

Chromium 155.0.8059.39.1 is now Stable on Linux (x64 and ARM64), Windows (x64), and macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel).

With a valid CloakBrowser key, the wrapper automatically selects the Stable build for your platform. No version pin is required.

What's new

  • The newest Chromium, 155, on every platform.
  • Windows and macOS catch up with Linux: safer proxy handling, the more patient license connection with the --license-route flag, and the refined Windows persona.
  • Closer to real Chrome everywhere: graphics checks, canvas exports, network timing, the reported CPU architecture on ARM hosts, and a few more Windows font names all behave the way real Chrome does on real hardware.
  • DNS that follows your proxy: with --fingerprint-transparent-proxy, sites are resolved with Cloudflare's DNS over HTTPS, sent through your proxy. Use your own with --fingerprint-transparent-proxy-dns=<url>, or local for the old behavior.
  • Clear license errors everywhere, a more stable macOS persona, quieter Windows security logs, and a smaller Linux download.

Your profiles, cookies, and seeds are untouched. Only the browser itself is replaced.

Current wrapper: v0.6.3

Update the wrapper before launching:

pip install -U cloakbrowser
npm update cloakbrowser
dotnet add package CloakBrowser --version 0.6.3

Roll back if needed

If a workload regresses, pin the previous Stable build for your platform:

export CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=154.0.8037.57.2   # Linux
export CLOAKBROWSER_VERSION=154.0.8037.57.1   # Windows, macOS

Remove the pin to return to the newest Stable build.

If you hit a regression, please tell us. Open an issue or email support@cloakbrowser.dev with the site and what you saw. Pinning the old build gets you unblocked; a report gets it fixed for everyone.

roboflow/supervision ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
0.31.1supervision-0.31.1 Stable2026-10-20T18:13:09Z

v0.31.1 — Recall that matches COCO, boxes that don't overflow

A bug-fix release: recall scores now agree with COCO, and half-precision boxes stop overflowing.

  • MeanAverageRecall skips crowd regions and matches predictions in confidence order, like pycocotools.
  • COCO segmentations loaded without an area field no longer make mAP return -1.
  • float16 boxes keep finite areas, and mAP and with_nmm stop overflowing on narrow coordinate types.
  • Mask and halo annotators draw on grayscale scenes, and vertex annotators accept (x, y, z) points.
  • Without OpenCV, ellipses and thick circles render like OpenCV 5, and grayscale images save correctly.

Drop-in upgrade, no code changes. mAR values can move: up on COCO data with crowd annotations, and in either direction where confidence order now decides which prediction claims a target.

✨ Spotlights / highlights

Recall that matches COCO

sv.metrics.MeanAverageRecall used to count COCO crowd regions as missed objects and to pair predictions with the highest-IoU target first. It now leaves out targets with data["iscrowd"] or data["ignore"] set, the same rule MeanAveragePrecision uses. It also matches predictions in descending confidence order with COCO's tie rule, and counts an oriented-box IoU of exactly 0.55, 0.6, 0.8 or 0.85 as a match at that threshold. One target, one crowd target and a perfect prediction now score 1.0 instead of 0.5. (#2750, #2758, #2752)

import numpy as np
import supervision as sv
from supervision.metrics import MeanAverageRecall

targets = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10], [20, 20, 30, 30]], dtype=float),
    class_id=np.array([0, 0]),
    data={"iscrowd": np.array([0, 1])},
)
predictions = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 10, 10]], dtype=float),
    class_id=np.array([0]),
    confidence=np.array([0.9]),
)
MeanAverageRecall().update(predictions, targets).compute().mAR_at_100  # 1.0

Half-precision boxes that stay finite

A 256×256 box in float16 has an area of 65,536, which is past float16's maximum, so Detections.box_area returned inf and area filters dropped it. Box areas of float16 detections are now computed and returned in float32, and MeanAveragePrecision and with_nmm no longer overflow on float16 or narrow integer coordinates either. COCO segmentations loaded with masks but without an area field now get it from the decoded mask, so those targets stay in their size bucket instead of turning mAP into -1. (#2764, #2743, #2753, #2763)

import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[0, 0, 256, 256], [0, 0, 0.01, 0.01]], dtype=np.float16)
)
detections.box_area  # array([6.5536000e+04, 1.0004273e-04], dtype=float32)

Grayscale scenes and 3D keypoints in annotators

sv.MaskAnnotator and sv.HaloAnnotator raised ValueError on single-channel images. They now accept (H, W), (H, W, 1) and Pillow "L" scenes, painting the gray value OpenCV would write for the same color. VertexAnnotator and the vertex-ellipse annotators draw (x, y, z) keypoints from their x and y, where they used to fail on tuple unpacking. (#2755, #2759)

import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

scene = np.zeros((100, 100), dtype=np.uint8)
mask = np.zeros((1, 100, 100), dtype=bool)
mask[0, 20:60, 20:60] = True
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[20, 20, 60, 60]], dtype=float), mask=mask, class_id=np.array([0])
)
sv.MaskAnnotator().annotate(scene.copy(), detections).shape  # (100, 100)

key_points = sv.KeyPoints(xy=np.array([[[10, 10, 0.5], [50, 50, 1.0]]], dtype=np.float32))
sv.VertexAnnotator().annotate(np.zeros((64, 64, 3), dtype=np.uint8), key_points)

Drawing without OpenCV, closer to OpenCV

The NumPy fallback used when OpenCV is not installed now ports OpenCV's ellipse rasterization, and thick circle outlines are centred on the radius instead of shrinking inward by half their thickness. Both match OpenCV 5.0 pixel for pixel in the reference tests. Without OpenCV, this changes the pixels drawn by EllipseAnnotator, RoundBoxAnnotator, the vertex-ellipse keypoint annotators, CircleAnnotator and DotAnnotator outlines. Image writing now accepts (H, W, 1) grayscale arrays and saves BGRA images as JPEG, and video reading handles files whose audio stream comes before the video stream. (#2740, #2765, #2754, #2746)

🔄 Migration guide

No migration required for this release.

📝 Notable changes

🔧 Fixed

MeanAverageRecall and COCO

  • sv.metrics.MeanAverageRecall counted COCO crowd and ignored targets as missed objects and paired predictions by highest IoU first; it now skips those targets and matches in descending confidence order with COCO's last-target tie rule, as COCO does. (#2750, #2758)
  • Oriented-box MeanAverageRecall, Precision, Recall and F1Score missed matches whose IoU was exactly 0.55, 0.6, 0.8 or 0.85, because the IoU was float64 and the thresholds float32. (#2752)

Overflow-safe boxes

  • Detections.box_area and box-based Detections.area overflowed to infinity for ordinary float16 boxes; they now compute and return float32. (#2764)
  • sv.metrics.MeanAveragePrecision overflowed box extents and areas for float16 or narrow integer coordinates, so perfect large boxes scored -1 or landed in the wrong size bucket. (#2743)
  • sv.Detections.with_nmm overflowed its area-weighted confidence for float16 boxes and, at extreme coordinates, for integer and float32 boxes. (#2753)
  • COCO loading with masks left segmented annotations without an area field with a NaN area, which pushed them out of every mAP size bucket; the area now comes from the decoded mask. (#2763)

Masks and polygons

  • resize_masks returned an empty array when downscaling very narrow masks; it now keeps at least one pixel per axis. (#2762)
  • sv.filter_polygons_by_area and sv.polygon_to_xyxy raised ValueError on empty polygons; they now treat them as zero area and an all-zero box. (#2761)

Annotators

  • sv.MaskAnnotator and sv.HaloAnnotator raised ValueError on grayscale scenes. (#2755)
  • VertexAnnotator and the vertex-ellipse annotators raised a tuple-unpacking error on three-coordinate keypoints; they now draw from x and y. (#2759)
  • sv.MaskAnnotator widened its blend region to the boxes of all-empty masks, including CompactMask, copying and blending outside the foreground. (#2741)

Without OpenCV

  • The fallback ellipse painted different pixels from OpenCV for thick strokes, fills and arcs; it now ports OpenCV's rasterization. (#2740)
  • The fallback circle grew thick outlines inward from the bounding box, shrinking them by half their thickness; they are now centred on the radius. (#2765)
  • Image writing rejected (H, W, 1) grayscale arrays and lost BGRA images saved as JPEG. (#2754)
  • Video reading failed on files whose audio stream comes before the first video stream. (#2746)

🏆 Contributors

Welcome to our first-time contributors, Ghanashyam V Narayan and jorge!

  • NIKHIL (@Nikhi00718) — fixed overflow in box areas, mAP and with_nmm, derived missing COCO areas, and fixed image writing and video reading without OpenCV.
  • Kaushik Reddy Lingireddy (@Lingikaushikreddy) — made MeanAverageRecall skip crowd targets and match by confidence, and fixed oriented-box threshold matching.
  • peng xiang (@px12811) — ported OpenCV's ellipse rasterization to the fallback and fixed mAR tie-breaking.
  • A Aswanth Raj (@aswanth-07) — fixed three-coordinate keypoint drawing and narrow-mask resizing.
  • Mohammad Hijjawi (@MohammadHijjawi97) — made MaskAnnotator and HaloAnnotator work on grayscale scenes.
  • kevin (@kevin9327) — centred thick fallback circles on their radius.
  • Ghanashyam V Narayan (@ghanashyam03) — made the polygon helpers accept empty polygons.
  • jorge (@jorge-asenjo) — kept empty compact masks out of the mask blend region.
  • Jirka Borovec (@Borda) — prepared the release.

Full changelog: https://github.com/roboflow/supervision/compare/0.31.0...0.31.1

sinelaw/fresh ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v0.5.4fresh-editor 0.5.4 Stable2026-10-20T18:11:22Z

0.5.4

For live updates on Fresh, follow me on X.

Most config options below can be changed in the Settings UI - run Open Settings from the command palette (Ctrl+P).

Features

  • Simple launch by default - based on your feedback, some defaults are dialed back so launching is simple. Nothing was removed (#3555, #3556, #3568, reported by @zipproth)
    • fresh FILE opens just that file, with no restored session, dock or Welcome tab (even if you left the dock open). This makes Fresh a better $EDITOR / git core.editor; fresh --simple does the same without a file
    • With Auto Attach on, a bare fresh is fresh -a (no name): the one shared background editor (a fresh -a that names a remote host, or finds a per-directory daemon already running in its directory, still goes to that one). Typed in a Fresh terminal, with Auto Attach on or off, either one now leaves that editor as it is and says you are already in it, instead of starting a second editor inside the terminal; fresh --simple, fresh -a NAME and piped input are refused there with an error. The message says how to start a separate editor anyway (FRESH_SESSION= fresh --simple)
    • Orchestrator mode is now Auto Attach (auto_attach): what the setting does is attach a bare fresh to the shared background editor, so it is named for that. orchestrator_mode in an existing config is still read, and moves to the new name the next time a setting is saved
    • The Orchestrator dock starts closed, for a bare fresh too and for existing users whose dock was open at their last quit; open it from View ▸ Orchestrator Dock and it stays open from then on
    • A bare fresh opens the directory you typed it in, also when it reattaches to a running daemon, instead of the workspace you used last. The new Open Last Workspace setting (open_last_workspace, off by default) brings back the old behaviour, with Auto Attach on or off
    • An empty workspace behaves the same for a bare fresh as in any launch: a [No Name] buffer on a first run, and closing the last tab follows auto_create_empty_buffer_on_last_buffer_close and file_explorer.auto_open_on_last_buffer_close instead of always leaving a blank pane
    • fresh DIR still restores that directory's previous workspace (open files, layout) and shows the Welcome tab; fresh --restore FILE does the same for a file launch
    • fresh DIR opens the file explorer unless you closed it in that directory yourself; fresh --simple (with or without a directory) starts with it closed
    • Startup is faster with many workspaces, which now load on first use
  • Markdown Source / Rendered / Source+Compose modes - new commands switch a Markdown pane between the raw text and the composed view, and a dual mode shows both side by side in one scroll-synced tab (edit on the source side; closing the tab leaves your file and panes as they were). "Cycle View Mode" steps through all three (#3562, by @PilotLeoYan)
  • Debian testing/unstable package - each release also attaches a .debian-testing.deb built from Debian's own packaged crates (#3519)
  • New config option: close a shell's tab when the shell exits - with it on, exit or Ctrl+D in an integrated terminal closes its tab (and the pane, if it was the only tab). Off by default; enable it in the Settings UI (#3537, by @cychitivav)
  • Middle-click closes a tab (#3284, #3286, by @CnsMaple)
  • Clickable "Palette: Ctrl+P" status hint opens the command palette (#3250, #3576, requested by @Korkman, by @peyton-durand)
  • Duplicate Line Above command, and duplicated lines keep carets and selections on the copy (#3244, by @kimprap)
  • Terminal programs can set your clipboard - OSC 52 writes from the integrated terminal reach the host clipboard (#3572, #3573, by @mycloa)

Bug Fixes

  • Unsaved changes carry over between the background daemon and a direct launch - an edit left unsaved in a bare fresh now comes back in fresh FILE or with Auto Attach off, and the other way round; each mode used to keep its own recovery store
  • A detached daemon no longer shuts itself down - it used to exit after an hour with no terminal attached, taking running agents with it; it now runs until you quit it
  • Markdown compose layout with emoji and CJK text - code-block frames keep their edges and wrapped table cells no longer start with a stray space or break early (#3562)
  • Clear error in mintty / Git Bash - Fresh now explains it needs a real console instead of failing with os error 6 (#3547, #3549, reported by @netoffice-zz)
  • git no longer hangs on a detached daemon - --wait against a daemon with nothing attached no longer waits on an invisible editor (#3555)
  • Plugin bundling uses a private temp directory, closing a local-user file-overwrite risk (#3557)
  • fresh -a works in deeply nested directories - the daemon no longer dies at startup when the directory path is too long for a Unix socket name; such directories get a shortened, hashed socket name, and every other directory keeps the name it had
  • macOS file-descriptor leak - the daemon no longer runs out of fds after files change in the project root (#3523, #3584, reported by @IconRunner05)
  • Windows fixes
    • formatters given as absolute paths (D:\...) are found again (#3281, #3289, by @CnsMaple)
    • Copy Path no longer pastes \\?\ prefixed paths (#3296, #3297, by @CnsMaple)
    • removing an Orchestrator worktree no longer fails with "Permission denied" (#3545)
  • Stale syntax colors after commenting a block of lines (#3551, by @kimprap)
  • Closing a discarded or saved last tab now closes its empty split (#3552, by @kimprap)
  • Rename works with servers lacking prepareRename, such as pylsp (#3540, by @cychitivav)
  • Regex replace keeps non-ASCII text in the replacement intact (#3571, by @neatsorg)
  • Unnamed buffers honor editor settings such as auto-close and occurrence highlight after restore (#3570, by @neatsorg)
  • A half-open client connection can't stall the daemon (#3542)
  • Hidden/ignored files are treated consistently across Quick Open, the explorer and project search (#3368, #3580, by @lixin-wei)
  • Bundled grammars load before bundle plugins (#3544)
  • Docs clarify textmate_grammar only supports .sublime-syntax (#3115, #3583, reported by @sgon00, by @peyton-durand)

Internals

  • Plugin buffer groups can show a file the user has open as an editable panel, with a new buffer_group_closed hook (#3560, #3562)
  • Virtual text always invalidates the wrap cache (#3311, #3485, by @anodicpassion); CI artifact usage reduced (#3577)

v0.9.93graphify 0.9.93 Stable2026-10-20T16:29:43Z

Twenty-two community pull requests. Extraction: a reference to a Kotlin type alias, C# delegate, Swift macro, Dart typedef, Python module function or Rust sibling-module use now resolves to its real declaration instead of minting a sourceless stub; Metal/CUDA GPU qualifiers no longer mint god nodes; extern "C" headers route to the C++ extractor; an extensionless script with a versioned-interpreter shebang is classified; and Obsidian vault-relative wikilinks resolve. Plus a credential-redaction pass on rationale labels, a node-confidence fold, a truncated-reply label decode, a .graphifyrc BOM fix, a GraphML multigraph export fix, two-repo file disambiguation in explain and path, a PDF-read warning, no skill writes on --version/--help, two PR-tooling fixes (slashed default branch, legacy CI statuses), and a skill partly-read-file recovery so a long file a subagent only skimmed is retried on the next --update instead of silently kept half-read. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

  • Fix: Kotlin a typealias declaration is extracted, so a field or parameter typed as the alias resolves to it instead of minting a sourceless cross-file stub (#4553, #4557, thanks @rajatnagda45).
  • Fix: C# a delegate declaration is extracted, so references resolve to it instead of a sourceless stub; built-in Func<>/Action<> stay external (#4552, #4556, thanks @rajatnagda45).
  • Fix: Swift macro declarations are extracted and a freestanding #macro(...) call resolves to the declaration; an unknown or standard-library macro stays unresolved rather than minting a stub (#4551, #4555, thanks @rajatnagda45).
  • Fix: Rust a use rooted at a sibling mod (for example use item::Thing;) now reaches its declaration, while an external use serde::... still does not hijack a same-named local type (#4564, #4567, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @almothafar-maf).
  • Fix: build a node's drifted or legacy confidence is folded onto the enum the same way edges and hyperedges already are, so a node no longer reaches graph.json with an unnormalized confidence (#4529, #4531, thanks @rudycelekli; reported by @grazenN).
  • Fix: llm community labels salvaged from a truncated reply are JSON-decoded, so an escaped label (\", \n, \uXXXX, surrogate pairs) is no longer kept with literal backslash escapes (#4537, thanks @rudycelekli).
  • Fix: rcfile .graphifyrc is read as utf-8-sig, so a file saved with a UTF-8 BOM no longer drops its first key (#4538, thanks @rudycelekli).
  • Fix: Dart a typedef is extracted as a type alias on its own line, including the legacy typedef R name(args) form, instead of a bogus variable of type typedef; a field or parameter typed by the alias resolves to it rather than minting a sourceless typedef stub (#4582, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).
  • Fix: Python a module.func() call resolves to the module child named exactly func, even when a same-key sibling (for example a FuncSchema class beside a func_schema function) previously made the lookup ambiguous and dropped the edge; it never binds to a same-named child of an unrelated module (#4577, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).
  • Fix: C++ Metal and CUDA GPU address/execution-space qualifiers (kernel, device, constant, __global__, __device__, ...) in a .metal/.cu file no longer mint sourceless god nodes; the kernel function still extracts and a <<<...>>> launch still resolves (#4550, #4554, thanks @rajatnagda45).
  • Fix: extract a .h header containing extern "C" is routed to the C++ extractor, so a C-API header the C grammar rejects extracts its symbols instead of nothing (#4526, thanks @bekzodibragimov2004-design).
  • Fix: extract credential-shaped text (API keys, tokens, Bearer tokens, private-key headers, user:pass@ URLs) in a comment or docstring that becomes a rationale label is redacted before it reaches graph.json, the viz or exports; ordinary identifiers such as git SHAs and UUIDs are left intact (#4566, thanks @0xkaushik-ai).
  • Fix: export GraphML export of a graph loaded as a MultiGraph (a graph with parallel edges, after #4500) no longer crashes with an empty output; parallel edges are written with distinct keys and round-trip through read_graphml (#4536, thanks @rudycelekli).
  • Fix: prs the default branch is derived by stripping only the refs/remotes/origin/ prefix, so a branch name that contains a slash (for example release/2.x) is kept whole and PRs against it are no longer all dropped as wrong-base (#4534, thanks @rudycelekli).
  • Fix: prs CI classification now reads legacy commit-status StatusContext state in addition to check-run conclusions, so a PR whose only signal is an external status (Jenkins, CircleCI) is classified correctly, with a failing status taking precedence (#4533, thanks @rudycelekli).
  • Fix: detect an extensionless script whose shebang names a versioned interpreter (#!/usr/bin/env python3.11, #!/bin/bash5, ruby3.2, ...) is now classified to its language instead of being skipped (#4535, thanks @rudycelekli).
  • Fix: detect when a PDF cannot be read (corrupt, encrypted, or a missing optional dependency) graphify prints a one-time warning naming the file instead of silently returning empty text, so a failed read is distinguishable from a text-less PDF (#4527, thanks @rudycelekli; reported by @grazenN).
  • Fix: markdown an Obsidian [[wikilink]] whose target begins with one of the scan root's own folder names (a vault-relative path) now resolves to the real page instead of a ghost node, restoring intra-vault connectivity (#4559, thanks @bercedev; reported by @CryptoRMac4).
  • Fix: explain / path two same-path files from different repos in a merged graph are kept distinct: an ambiguous name names each repo and the retry hint points at the full node id, instead of conflating them as one file (#4512, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @kaka-in-home).
  • Fix: cli graphify --version and --help no longer rewrite or back up an installed skill file; only a real command refreshes skills (the staleness warning still prints) (#4545, thanks @bercedev; reported by @EmanuelFaria).
  • Fix: query a bare name that is the exact name of several nodes (for example a .nonce() method in two files) is refused with the candidates listed and the ambiguous exit code, matching explain and path; a keyword that only prefix- or substring-matches labels still runs a normal search (#4511, #4517, thanks @shivampal46011; reported by @kaka-in-home).
  • Fix: skill a long file a subagent only partly read is no longer a silent, permanent loss. On the skill extraction path each chunk now self-reports the lines it covered; a file whose reported coverage falls short of its real length is written to .graphify_partial.txt, cached as partial (which the loader treats as a miss) and left unstamped in the manifest, so the next --update re-dispatches it and replace-on-re-extract swaps the half-read node set for a complete one. This mirrors the library path's truncated-reply recovery (#933, #1950); the already-extracted nodes are kept, and a file no subagent reported is not falsely flagged (#3987, #2225, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @Ryanm218).

astral-sh/uv ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
0.13.4 Stable2026-10-20T15:24:59Z

Release Notes

Released on 2026-10-20.

This release addresses GHSA-hq85-5cpj-mr62, which involves a root CA whose intermediate on the Web PKI have been compromised. Users are encouraged to upgrade immediately, as well as confirm that all other software that uses bundled CAs is also properly updated.

Preview features

  • Validate PEP 825 variant metadata and treat package versions with invalid metadata as unavailable under wheel-variants (#22512)

Other changes

  • Update the bundled Mozilla root certificates via webpki-root-certs 1.0.10 (#22760)

Install uv 0.13.4

Install prebuilt binaries via shell script

curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.13.4/uv-installer.sh | sh

Install prebuilt binaries via powershell script

powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.13.4/uv-installer.ps1 | iex"
